summary: The blueprint is broadly plausible for healthy human pancreas but needs targeted additions for missing resident neural/glial and possibly mesothelial/capsular populations plus small marker refinements.

issues.description: No axis captures pancreatic neural/glial cells, especially Schwann/peripheral glial populations that can appear in whole-pancreas atlases.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a grounded Schwann/peripheral glial module and plain axis with markers such as SOX10, S100B, PLP1, MPZ, GFRA3, NGFR, and/or GAP43.

issues.description: No axis represents mesothelial/capsular serosal cells, a small but distinct whole-pancreas population not well captured by ductal or fibroblast axes.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a mesothelial/capsular epithelial module and plain axis if supportable from qualifying literature, using markers such as MSLN, WT1, UPK3B, KRT19, KRT8, KRT18, and CALB2.

issues.description: The single broad ductal axis may blur ductal/centroacinar bicarbonate-transport programs and larger-duct mucinous programs in whole-pancreas data.
issues.suggested_fix: Either enrich the existing ductal module with stronger duct/centroacinar functional markers such as CFTR, SLC4A4, SLC26A6, ANXA4, TFF1, or MUC1 where supported, or add a separate centroacinar/ductal-refinement axis if literature support is strong.

issues.description: The epsilon module is very small and includes generic endocrine genes, so it may mostly reflect endocrine-core signal plus GHRL rather than specifically resolving rare ghrelin/epsilon cells.
issues.suggested_fix: Strengthen the module with additional supported ghrelin/epsilon markers if available, or reduce generic endocrine genes in favor of more specific markers while retaining the axis.

out_of_scope: Citation and DOI verification were not reassessed; this report judges biological plausibility and coverage only.
